meta.title: How a scoped rule fires: an illustrative 3-in-10-second threshold

cards.title: Illustrative records, not a measured trace
items: Assume one qualified capture/source scope, capture_time mode, type TCP, expression SYN, threshold 3, threshold_window 10 and group_by [SrcIP]. A and B are two distinct source IPs; the relative times are synthetic.

Messages show the order in which records are released for evaluation. Actual capture-time mode buffers up to configured lateness; finalization drains pending records before readiness (docs/RULES_ENGINE.md:63-71).

cards.title: Why exactly one alert appears
items: Only expression matches reach threshold counting. Group keys include scope, rule name and configured fields (engine.go:320-388; scoped.go:34-36,46-100).
At t=6, A's matching observations are at 1, 4 and 6 seconds. B's match and A's ACK-only record do not contribute to A's threshold.
The window boundary is inclusive. A crossing deletes that group's count state; it does not consume another group's history (scoped.go:68-98).

cards.title: Conditions outside this example
items: An optional sequence precondition runs before threshold counting. Wall-clock deduplication and rate limiting are not the scoped counting model shown here (engine.go:330-427).

Missing grouping fields, ambiguous scope, excessive lateness or state capacity can withhold or fail evaluation. A threshold configuration alone does not prove capture coverage (docs/RULES_ENGINE.md:63-77).
